newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian politicians meet on jumbo TV package.
newsitem.headline: Italian politicians meet on jumbo TV package.

text.p: Italy's ruling centre-left coalition met on Monday to discuss a jumbo package of measures for the broadcasting sector to replace other decrees due to expire soon.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi, Post and Communications Minister Antonio Maccanico and his deputy Vincenzo Vita were taking part in the meeting, officials said.
The opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance, led by media mogul Silvio Berlusconi, is due to meet later on Monday to discuss the government's planned measures.

Vita told La Repubblica newspaper the government had already made concessions to the Freedom Alliance and the jumbo amendment was its best offer. "It's the last day, take it or leave it," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

He did not rule out the government putting the package to a confidence test, but said if there were no agreement with the Freedom Alliance, the ruling coalition would present its own text, "not a compromise".

The package will be examined by the Culture and Transport and Communications Commissions of the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Tuesday. A joint meeting of the commissions had been scheduled for Monday to examine the planned measures.
The government said last week an umbrella amendment to unify three broadcasting decrees should be approved by Christmas.
The decrees include one which would extend broadcasting licences due to expire at the end of January and which mainly concerns Berlusconi's Mediaset three TV stations.
The package also contains measures to safeguard state broadcaster RAI.
The three decrees rolled into the jumbo package were all due to expire before Christmas.
The umbrella amendment is the result of an initial accord reached last week between the government and the Freedom Alliance to extend the January expiry of licences until the end of May next year.
The Constitutional Court ruled two years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels and set August 1996 as the deadline for changes to be implemented.

The government extended the current ownership rules until the end of January 1997 after that deadline passed in order to plug a legal gap in which magistrates could technically have forced Berlusconi to take one of his channels off the air.
The government has presented a bill to shake up the sector, but it has been held up in parliament by disagreement over a part of the bill concerning telecommunications.
